title: Record a PR per issue, open it via gh pr create, show live state in status

verified_files.detail: normalize_pr_ref, parse_pr_rows, render_pr_table, record_pr, query_pr_state, refresh_pr_states, plus a record/refresh CLI. Every gh call has a 5s timeout and returns None on any failure.
18 tests; gh is mocked in all of them.
Ships an empty sentinel-wrapped Pull Requests block.
Step 5 records the PR it already opens (gh pr create was added by E02-ISS-02).
Displays PR state explicitly as last-known, never as live truth.

design_decisions.decision: A managed '## Pull Requests' section, not a table column.
design_decisions.why: The issue table is parsed by column index by five consumers, and sync_metrics.split_row discards empty cells, so a blank PR cell would shift every index after it. The section is only viable because E03-ISS-01 stopped the metric splice truncating to EOF.

design_decisions.decision: gh is optional: 5s timeout, None on every failure, cached state preserved.
design_decisions.why: gh may be missing, unauthenticated, offline or slow. A missing gh must degrade to 'PR recorded, state unknown', never to a failed verify or a wrong state. All eight failure modes are tested.

design_decisions.decision: Refresh is on demand, never a hook.
design_decisions.why: A hook shelling out to gh on every edit would put network latency on the edit path.
A stale OPEN on a merged PR is worse than showing nothing.

definition_of_done.criterion: All tests pass; full suite green
record_pr then sync() leaves both the PR section and the metric blocks correct
definition_of_done.evidence: Tested, and verified on a copy of the real board: record then two consecutive syncs keep both sentinels, all rows, and correct totals

definition_of_done.criterion: Every gh failure mode yields None and preserves recorded state
definition_of_done.evidence: Eight modes covered: missing binary, non-zero exit, timeout, unparseable JSON, empty output, unrecognised state, missing key, OSError

definition_of_done.criterion: Recording against a CLOSED board is refused
definition_of_done.evidence: RuntimeError raised and the file left byte-identical

definition_of_done.criterion: This session's PR #4 is recorded for the issues it closes and refresh reports its real state
definition_of_done.evidence: All 8 closed E-03 issues recorded against #4; refresh queried the live PR and returned OPEN for each. Committed state verified via git show.
verify-issue step 5 records; status presents last-known state and says so when gh is unreachable

definition_of_done.criterion: A block whose start sentinel was stripped still parses and preserves rows
definition_of_done.evidence: Found during verification; see environmental_finding. Two regression tests added.

environmental_finding.what: The installed plugin cache runs a pre-E03-ISS-01 sync_metrics.py as its PostToolUse Edit|Write hook. That version truncates the sprint board at '## Time & Velocity Summary' to EOF, so a single Edit-tool call deletes the entire Pull Requests section.
environmental_finding.proof: Recorded the block (start sentinel present), made one unrelated Edit to a spec file, then re-counted: start=0 end=0. The whole block was gone. The repo's own sync_metrics.py preserves it across repeated syncs, confirmed on a copy of the real board.
environmental_finding.consequence: Until `/plugin update solorail` refreshes the cache, every Edit-tool call in this repo destroys content below the velocity summary. The code is correct; the hook firing is ten commits behind it.
environmental_finding.mitigation_applied: Recorded the PRs and committed in a single Bash invocation, and wrote this receipt via shell rather than the Edit tool. Committed state verified with `git show HEAD:...`.
environmental_finding.code_hardening: parse_pr_rows now also enters on the '## Pull Requests' heading, not only the start sentinel. Requiring the sentinel meant a block damaged this way silently lost every recorded row on the next write -- real data loss, found only because the damage happened for real.

notes: The epic criterion asked for gh pr create in verify-issue; E02-ISS-02 had already added it, so this issue supplied the missing half -- recording and displaying. The plugin-cache staleness is the highest-value remaining item: it actively destroys sprint-board content on every edit.
